notes: “Eunuchs” names a royal court office. The passage does not explicitly say that these young men were physically made eunuchs.
The text says that the food and wine would defile Daniel but does not state the precise reason. The draft does not insert an explanation.
The requested food is what grows from seed and may include more than modern vegetables. Verse 15 describes fuller flesh, not simply an abstract claim of better health.
The statement that Daniel remained until Cyrus’s first year does not say that he died in that year.
vocabulary: A biblical name associated with Babylonia.
The official assigns Babylonian names: Belteshazzar to Daniel, Shadrach to Hananiah, Meshach to Mishael, and Abed-nego to Azariah.

notes: The Hebrew description of the king’s sleep is idiomatic and somewhat difficult. The draft understands his sleep as leaving him.

The book changes from Hebrew to Aramaic after the introductory words “in Aramaic.” This Aramaic section continues beyond this chapter. The reading note has singular “your servant,” where the written form is plural; the following “we” is retained.
The expression rendered as a firm decision is disputed. It has also been understood to mean that the matter or dream has gone from the king. The draft does not state that he forgot the dream.
The participle can describe an execution underway or the situation created by the death order. Verse 24 still speaks of stopping the destruction; the draft does not infer how many had already died.
“We will tell” preserves Daniel’s plural wording after his statement that this was the dream.
The kingdoms following Nebuchadnezzar are not named in the speech. Their later historical identification is not inserted into the translation.
“Human offspring” renders the image of human seed. Intermarriage is one way of understanding the attempted mixture, but the text does not state the precise arrangement.
The king bows before Daniel and orders an offering and incense for him. The draft preserves the action without adding a refusal that the narrative does not record.
vocabulary: Here a group of court specialists, rather than simply all the inhabitants of Babylonia.
The royal officer overseeing the men who carry out death sentences; the title literally concerns slaughtering.
Something hidden that becomes known through divine disclosure.
